reserves.issuerOrObligor: Selected commercial banks and broker-dealers; Treasury obligations as collateral

sources.label: KPMG PYUSD Redemption Assets Report - July 2026 (examination dated August 25, 2026)

reserveReview.rationale: Exhibit B of the KPMG-examined PYUSD report at July 31, 2026 records $94,699,538 cash, $2,200,625,000 Treasury-collateralized reverse repos and $398,747,625 Treasury bills, totaling $2,694,072,163. Rounded weights are 3.52%, 81.68% and 14.80%. The repos mature August 3, three calendar days after the Friday observation, despite being described as overnight; collateral may not be sold or repledged. The three Treasury bills mature August 18, August 27 and September 17, a maximum of 48 days after period end. No government money-market funds were held.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: KPMG examination of the PYUSD Redemption Assets Report, Exhibit B as of July 31, 2026
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: The report identifies the complete asset-type composition. Individual commercial-bank and broker-dealer counterparties are anonymized, but no reserve asset class is unclassified.

sources.label: KPMG PYUSD Redemption Assets Report - May 2026

custodyProfile.uncertainty: The KPMG-examined report establishes segregated, unencumbered redemption assets held on behalf of PYUSD token holders by Paxos Trust Company, N.A., an OCC-supervised national trust bank, and prohibits selling or repledging the securities collateralizing the repo agreements. The Paxos USD Stablecoin Terms (last modified June 30, 2026, section 3.2.3.1) state that assets held with Paxos Trust are held bankruptcy remote and would not be used to satisfy Paxos Trust debts in insolvency; that fiduciary custody structure supports the structured bankruptcy-remoteness grade. Individual banks, the qualified custodian, and repo counterparties are not named, per-account placement is not published, and rehypothecation terms for cash deposits are not established, so the mixed cash and repo envelope stays conditional.
